title: kv cache: adaptive eviction + defragmentation to reduce spillover under high-concurrency
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Reduced KV cache spillover under high-concurrency workloads; improved memory fragmentation handling and adaptive paging thresholds. No API changes.
description: Motivation: Under sustained high-concurrency workloads we observed increased KV cache spillover and memory fragmentation which degrades latency and increases downstream paging. This PR introduces an adaptive eviction policy combined with a periodic defragmentation/compaction pass and tuning to paging thresholds to reduce spillover events. Summary of changes: 1) Adaptive eviction: combine recency (LRU) with token-age weighting so long-lived large KV entries are considered for early eviction under memory pressure. 2) Defragmentation/compaction: a background compaction pass that coalesces freed pages within kernel-managed allocator to reduce fragmentation and lower peak resident set. 3) Paging/spillover tuning: dynamic thresholds based on observed allocation churn and current scheduler batch sizes to defer spill-to-disk until absolutely necessary. 4) Exposed runtime flags and metrics: kv_cache.compactions, kv_cache.evictions_by_policy, kv_cache.spillover_events, kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio. 5) Tests and integration: unit tests, integration load test, and canary rollout config. Checklist: - [x] Design doc in Linear (ENG-4821) - [x] Unit tests for eviction and defrag logic - [x] Integration test simulating 2k concurrent short-lived requests - [x] Metrics and tracing hooks added - [x] Canary rollout to Dedicated + Hosted small subset - [x] Backfill docs (docs/kv_cache.md) Backport: This change touches allocator behavior; plan to backport to release/2025-q4 for Dedicated customers. No public API changes; default behavior unchanged unless flags enabled. Security/Compliance: No secrets or RPC surface added. Notes: tuning parameters are conservative by default; operators can opt-in to more aggressive compaction in private deployments. Linear refs: ENG-4821 (design), ENG-4940 (canary analysis).

review_comments: Daniel Kim (2025-11-04): Nice clear design. Two questions: 1) how do we avoid compaction pauses impacting p99? 2) can we provide a non-default conservative config?

Asha Patel (2025-11-04): For compaction we use an incremental background pass with a max-wall-time budget per cycle; added 'compaction.max_ms_per_cycle' flag and described in docs. Default config is conservative; operators must opt-in for aggressive mode.
Lena Rodriguez (2025-11-06): Can you add a metric for bytes reclaimed per compaction cycle and a histogram of compaction duration? That will help tuning during canary.
Asha Patel (2025-11-06): Added kv_cache.compaction_bytes_reclaimed and kv_cache.compaction_duration_ms histogram. Updated metrics dashboard snapshot in the PR description.
Samuel Ortiz (2025-11-08): Ran the integration test locally; saw a rare race on shutdown. Please take a look at teardown ordering.
Asha Patel (2025-11-09): Fixed teardown race (commit f6b22d3). Reran CI; all green. Marking for final review.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2025-11-12 by Asha Patel (squash merge).
summary_perf: Canary results: 40% reduction in spillover_events, 18% lower p99 token latency at 2k concurrent requests, and ~12% reduction in peak GPU memory usage attributed to compaction. CPU overhead of compaction < 3% in observed runs.
